written.myAnswer: Temperature-dependent solubility is useful for purifying solids by crystallization. The lower solubility of gases at higher temperatures also helps keep gases such as carbon dioxide dissolved when solutions are cooled.
Different compounds have different solubilities because their chemical nature and interactions with water differ.
NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature, whereas KNO₃ solubility increases greatly. So cooling a hot saturated solution does not crystallize NaCl from water in the same way.

Solubility is the amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent at a particular temperature. The solubility of most solids increases with temperature, although some change little or decrease; the solubility of gases in water generally decreases.
Dissolve the impure KNO₃ in a minimum amount of hot water to form a saturated solution. Allow it to cool so KNO₃ crystallizes, then separate the crystals from the remaining solution and dry them.
